text: Since you haven't reported changes in urine or stool color yet, I need to verify this with objective data given your heavy alcohol use and weight loss. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panels and REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound. Do you have any personal or family history of blood disorders or liver disease?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Function Tests: AST Elevated, ALT Elevated, ALP Significantly elevated, Bilirubin Elevated. Urine Analysis: Appearance Amber, Bilirubin Positive. Abdominal Ultrasound: Findings show an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder with no evident stones.

speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: The ultrasound showing an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones, combined with your significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin, strongly suggests an obstruction. Given your history of heavy smoking and unintentional weight loss, do you have any family history of pancreatic cancer or have you noticed a palpable mass in your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient does not report any fever, abdominal pain, or changes in bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the painless jaundice, weight loss, and the enlarged, non-stony gallbladder on ultrasound, I suspect a malignant obstruction at the pancreatic head. To confirm this suspicion, REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pancreas and REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Abdomen (Pancreas): Hypodense mass (3.5 cm) identified in the head of the pancreas causing dilation of the common bile duct and pancreatic duct (double duct sign). No evidence of distant metastasis on current imaging. Regional lymphadenopathy noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan confirms a 3.5 cm mass in the head of your pancreas causing a double duct sign, which is highly indicative of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. To determine if the tumor is resectable and to stage the disease accurately, I will order a tissue biopsy and check your CA 19-9 tumor marker levels. REQUEST TEST: Endoscopic_Ultrasound_with_Biopsy and REQUEST TEST: CA_19-9. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma.
